subject: Service retrospective and assurance packet — Sylvan Bank April 20 event
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@sylvanbank.com>
Cc: Sylvan Bank Tech <tech@sylvanbank.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service retrospective and assurance packet — Sylvan Bank April 20 event

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for your patience while our team completed the internal analysis of the April 20th performance degradation that impacted parts of your inference workload. Attached is a concise assurance packet intended for Sylvan's compliance and engineering teams. The attachment bundle contains: 

- sylvan-retrospective-summary.pdf — high-level narrative, findings, and customer-facing commitments
- event-timeline.csv — minute-level events from Redwood's control plane and selected service metrics
- mitigation-runbook-v1.2.md — operational steps we will run in a future automated play to prevent recurrence

Executive summary (top-level):
- What happened: A partial KV-cache eviction cascade triggered by a telemetry-backed scaling job caused increased token re-generation and transient request spikes across a subset of model backends. This produced elevated latencies and a small number of failed requests for customers on MultiPool-1.
- Root cause (short): An interaction between an autoscaler job and a cache eviction heuristic during an unusually high prefix-duplication workload. The job over-estimated memory pressure and evicted shared prefix segments in a handful of serving instances.
- Impact to Sylvan: Approximately 0.6% of inference calls from your production tier observed latency > 5s; 0.03% returned a 5xx within the 40-minute window. No customer data exposure or token leakage was detected in our audit.
- Immediate fixes applied: We rolled back the autoscaler heuristic, applied soft-guard thresholds, and executed a targeted warm-up to rebuild KV prefixes for the affected pool.

Requested next steps for your team:
1) Review the attached packet and confirm if you need a redacted copy for internal audit.
2) If useful, we can present a 30-45 minute technical walkthrough for Sylvan's platform and compliance teams next week.

If you prefer, I can also extract only the timeline and runbook for your internal SREs. We're prepared to share additional logs under our NDA/secure transfer if Sylvan needs deeper forensic artifacts. 

Would Thursday 10:00–11:00 PT work for a walkthrough?

Thanks,

— Soojin Lee
Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference
attachments: sylvan-retrospective-summary.pdf (pdf), event-timeline.csv (csv), mitigation-runbook-v1.2.md (text)
From: Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@sylvanbank.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Sylvan Bank Tech <tech@sylvanbank.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 12:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Service retrospective and assurance packet — Sylvan Bank April 20 event

Soojin,

Thanks for the packet — we appreciate the level of detail. Quick questions after a first pass: 

1) Can you add a short item (one or two lines) in the summary explicitly confirming there was no PII exfiltration or token leakage? We need that sentence for our compliance folder.
2) The timeline CSV looks useful, but can you call out the rows where the autoscaler executed (timestamp + instance id)? We want to map those to our request traces.
3) For the runbook: can you add an immediate mitigation we can trigger from our side (a config flag) if we detect a similar pattern? Having a defensive knob we control is important for our ops SLA.

We'd like the walkthrough but prefer a call with your engineering lead + someone from platform. Thurs 10:00 PT works; please send an invite.

Elena
Head of Platform Reliability
Sylvan Bank

Cc: Sylvan Bank Tech <tech@sylvanbank.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service retrospective and assurance packet — Sylvan Bank April 20 event

Hi Elena — thank you for the quick review and clear asks. Attached are the items you requested: 

- sylvan-retrospective-summary.pdf (updated): added explicit confirmation: “Redwood confirms no PII exfiltration or token leakage was observed in our audits of the impacted instances.”
- event-timeline.csv (updated): added 'autoscaler_exec' boolean column and instance_id column; rows with autoscaler runs are highlighted in the first column.
- mitigation-runbook-v1.2.md: appended a short defensive knob your SREs can flip (documented as CUSTOMER_DEFENSIVE_KNOB=false|true). When enabled it disables cross-instance shared-kv eviction for your customer pool and forces local warm-up; we describe expected behavior and rollback steps.

Meeting: Thurs Apr 29, 2027 10:00–10:45 PT (invite sent). Agenda: 1) 10m executive summary, 2) 20m technical deep dive (timeline + forensic mapping), 3) 10m mitigation knob and runbook Q&A, 4) 5m next steps and evidence transfer.

Deliverables we will provide during/after the call: 
- Redacted logs for the two most critical instances (secure transfer link posted in meeting notes)
- A follow-up verification plan with dates for the automated guard thresholds and the runbook rehearse
- A post-verification note stating the closure criteria from both parties

If you need anything earlier, please ping me directly. 

Best,

— Soojin Lee
Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference
